To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the magnitude of gluonic shadowing at RHIC is comparable to the magnitude of nonperturbative nuclear shadowing, while at LHC perturbative gluonic shadowing dominates over the magnitude of non-perturbative shadowing.

(i) the different perturbatively-based models for gluon shadowing predict similar magnitude of shadowing for the kinematics of RHIC and LHC, (ii) at LHC, the magnitude of pertubative gluon shadowing is comparable to nonperturbative gluon shadow, and (iii) the uncertainties in gluons shadowing coming from different parametrizations of gluon distributions are larger than those coming from different models for gluon perturbative shadow

the predictions of the perturbative QED-based models for nuclear gluon shadowing are similar at RHIC but they can differ significantly at LHC, and that the uncertainties in the magnitude of gluonic shadowing coming from different parametrizations of gluon distributions in nucleons are much larger than those due the different models of gluon nuclear shadowing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the nuclear gluon distribution function in the region of small values of Bjorken x.
the study of gluon shadow in the nuclear medium.
the study of the gluon structure of the nucleus and the effects of nuclear shadowing on the production of jets and heavy quarkonia in relativistic heavy ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, at present, the uncertainty in the magnitude of nuclear gluon shadowing is dominated by the uncertainty in the gluon distribution inside nucleons.

at the kinematics of RHIC, all perturbative QED-based models of shadowing give similar estimates of shadowing, and the magnitude of pertur-bative shadowing is comparable to that of nonperturbative gluon shadowing.

the magnitude of pertur-bative gluon shadowing is not well known at the present time, and it is not clear whether the difference between the different models is due to a real physical phenomenon or to the uncertainties in the input parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the uncertainties in the magnitude of nuclear shadowing coming from different perturbative models and from different nucleon gluon distributions are comparable and larger than uncertainties coming from nonperturbative initial shadowing.
the gluon shadowing at LHC is large, but its precise value is still uncertain.
the gluon shadowing effects at the BNL relativisitc heavy ion collider and at the CERN large hadronic collider are large enough to have a significant impact on the physics of these experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uncertainties due to different parametrization are larger than those coming from different models of perturbative QED.
at RHIC and LHC, perturbative QED models of gluon nuclear shadowing are not very sensitive to the parametrization of gluon distributions in the proton.
, at the present level of understanding of gluon shadowings, one cannot distinguish between different gluon shadowing models by comparing their predictions to the data on nuclear structure functions.
